subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Spitfire model in cyanotype blueprint style with blue background and white outlines, using real-world proportions (9.1m length, 11.2m wingspan, ~3.5m height) with the nose facing +Z and landing gear down, keeping it static and reasonably efficient to build.

I'm calculating ground clearance for the propeller tip based on gear height, then planning the loft-based fuselage construction with stations along the z-axis for width and height.

Defining station coordinates...

Still working out the wing outline geometry...

I'm checking that the mirrored outline still produces correct winding when extruded, and deciding to use a constant thickness with a small bevel rather than tapering along the chord. For wing placement, I'm positioning it as a low-wing configuration slightly below the fuselage centerline, checking the fuselage's bottom edge against the wing root height.

Now I'm working out the gear geometry: splayed main wheels at the wing tips with rods angling outward to the hubs, setting wheel radius and thickness so they just touch the ground, plus a small tail wheel with its own strut positioned near the tail of the fuselage.

I'm adding details like wing gun bumps, the asymmetric oil cooler and radiator pods under the wings, and roundel decals rendered as concentric circle textures on flat planes placed on top of the wing surfaces.

Now I'm working out the tail fin geometry, extruding an outline in the local z-y plane to get the vertical fin shape with correct orientation relative to the fuselage axis.

Still shaping fin outline coordinates... Now I'm moving on to the tailplane, planning a small elliptical shape extruded like the wing with a half-span of 1.7 and chord of 1.0.

For the propeller, I'm setting up three blades spaced 120 degrees apart, computing direction vectors for each blade angle, and sketching tapered blade outlines along the hub.

Now I'm adding a conical spinner tip aligned along the +Z axis, sizing it to fit the nose radius smoothly where the propeller shaft meets the fuselage.

Next I'm placing six small exhaust stack cylinders along each side of the cowl, angled outward and back, embedded into the fuselage surface near the nose.

For the canopy, I'm using a scaled sphere as the bubble glass, giving it a pale blue tint to suggest translucent glass in the cyanotype style.

Placing the ribs along the canopy at different z-positions, scaling each by the ellipsoid's cross-sectional radius so they hug the curved surface. I'll skip the windscreen detail and extra ground grid for now, keeping the focus on the cyanotype-style base paint treatment.

For the hull paint, I'm blending a pale-blue top with darker undersides based on surface normal, overlaying grid lines spaced at regular intervals, plus panel lines, roundels, and stencil serial text like "K9942" rendered via SVG for that blueprint look. Writing hull paint function...

Adding fuselage ring lines, blueprint-style palette colors, and flat material definitions for props and glass canopy. I'm also planning decal overlays on the wings for aileron seams, rivets, and roundel markings to add surface detail.

For fuselage detailing, I'm positioning a fin flash decal with vertical stripe bars on the rudder, plus text and roundel decals placed on the fuselage sides using surface-mounted decal projections at specific offsets.

I'll skip worrying about mirroring for the roundel and code text, assuming the decals read correctly as drawn from the viewing direction. With exhaust and guns placed, I'm now adding cannon barrel stubs as short cylinders in the wing leading edge, positioning them near the wingtips based on the leading-edge curve geometry.

Since the wing lacks a proper airfoil thickness profile, I'll leave that detail simple and focus on the root fairing. For the radiators under the wing, I'm considering using scaled sphere shapes positioned beneath the wing surface in paint color, checking that they clear the wing's bottom boundary.

Checking the fuselage cross-section at z=0 confirms it dips lower than the wing's underside, so no intersection there. I'm now computing the wingtip outline points, spacing leading-edge coordinates across the span and avoiding a degenerate zero-chord point right at the tip by stopping just short of the maximum span value.

Setting root chord and offsets using sample values, I'm sanity-checking against a real Spitfire's rough proportions, then planning a reusable wing-planform function parameterized by half-span, root chord, and sweep so I can reuse it for the tailplane with smaller dimensions, mirroring the shape across the x-axis for the opposite side.

Positioning the tailplane, fin, exhaust, pitot probe, and antenna mast on the fuselage, checking that each part's placement sits flush against the body without overlapping gaps.

Maybe rivets too, keeping it minimal. For the roundel placement on the wings, I'm computing the chord geometry at that span position to center it properly, and figuring out the orientation so the texture reads correctly from a top-down view.

Skipping underside roundel for now. For the fin flash, I'm working out the fin's thickness and outline coordinates to position a striped decal plane roughly centered on the fin surface.

Now I'm setting up the paint helper and starting the Three.js import for placing decals.

I'm defining a bluePaint function that blends deep and light tones based on surface lighting, then adds grid lines with a texel density scaled to the painted surface area.

Tuning grid line widths and spacing for minor and major lines, then adding separate panel-line paint for the fuselage with periodic rings and longitudinal seams using a distance helper function. I'm also noting that static parts like the fuselage loft don't need bone joints since they're not animated.

Now I'm working out the geometry for wheels and landing gear—cylindrical tires with hubs, dark tire color, strut rods connecting the leg to the wheel, and a simple fairing box around the leg, making sure the wheel bottoms line up at the ground plane.

Adding the tailwheel, checking the level attitude so all contact points sit flush, then placing the prop tip height. I'm positioning exhaust stubs along the cowl using small cylinders angled outward, coloring them a pale blue-white, sizing the radiators asymmetrically under each wing, and shaping the spinner as a cone at the nose.

Placing the propeller plane so blades intersect the spinner naturally, then designing an SVG roundel with concentric stroked circles and a monospace "QV·K" decal to apply onto the fuselage surface, plus varying the hull color slightly between topside and underside.
